question:
The radius and height of a cylindrical container are measured as $7\ \text{cm}$ and $10\ \text{cm}$, respectively. The possible errors in these measurements are $0.01\ \text{cm}$ and $0.02\ \text{cm}$, respectively.

(a) Using differentials, estimate the maximum error in the calculated volume.

(b) Determine the corresponding relative error.

(c) Calculate the percentage error in the volume.
explanation:
(a)
The volume of the cylinder is
$$V=\pi r^2h$$
Its differential is
$$dV=2\pi rh\,dr+\pi r^2\,dh$$
For the maximum approximate error, take the magnitudes of the measurement errors.
$$|dV|=2\pi(7)(10)(0.01)+\pi(7)^2(0.02)$$
$$|dV|=1.4\pi+0.98\pi$$
$$|dV|=2.38\pi\ \text{cm}^3$$

(b)
Dividing the differential of the volume by $V=\pi r^2h$,
$$\frac{|dV|}{V}=2\frac{|dr|}{r}+\frac{|dh|}{h}$$
Substituting the given values,
$$\frac{|dV|}{V}=2\left(\frac{0.01}{7}\right)+\frac{0.02}{10}$$
$$\frac{|dV|}{V}=\frac{1}{350}+\frac{1}{500}=\frac{17}{3500}$$
Thus, the approximate relative error is $\frac{17}{3500}$.

(c)
The percentage error is
$$\frac{17}{3500}\times 100=\frac{17}{35}\%$$
$$\frac{17}{35}\%\approx 0.486\%$$
